title: Mark Cuban Says Meta and Google Could Be Funding Their AI Future With Anti-Tech Content: 'Interesting to Watch the Irony…'

On Monday, billionaire investor Mark Cuban warned that social media algorithms could amplify anti-AI sentiment even as companies like Meta Platforms, Inc. and Alphabet Inc. pour billions of dollars into building and promoting artificial intelligence.

Mark Cuban on Social Media's AI Paradox

Cuban made the comments on X, arguing that social media algorithms could create an unexpected problem for companies developing AI.

"I think it's going to be interesting to watch the irony of the social media algos amplifying the [anti-AI] sentiment far beyond any positive AI sentiment," Cuban wrote.

He added that Meta and Google could end up "trying to make enough money from pushing people to hate AI, to subsidize their AI."

Meta and Google did not immediately respond to Benzinga's request for comment.

I think it's going to be interesting to watch the irony of the social media algos amplifying the anti AI sentiment far beyond any positive AI sentiment.

Meta and Google are going to be trying to make enough money from pushing people to hate AI, to subsidize their AI

— Mark Cuban (@mcuban) September 15, 2026

A user responding to Cuban argued that algorithms do not need to be explicitly anti-AI. Instead, they may simply learn that fear, anger and anxiety over AI keep users engaged longer than positive content.

Cuban replied, "I look at those as being the same."

I look at those as being the same.

— Mark Cuban (@mcuban) September 15, 2026

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

Cuban Sees Bigger Risk In Human Reactions

In a follow-up post, Cuban expanded on his argument, saying frontier AI companies may have powerful models but lack control over the social media systems that determine what content goes viral.

He said he believes there is a "far greater risk from what humans do in response to what they see on social media than what agent swarms will do."

Cuban added that the equation could change if AI agents eventually gain control of social media algorithms.

Which will lead to the ultimate irony. The frontier labs, without social media platforms, have the most powerful AI. But it's not powerful enough to reverse engineer the social media algorithms and push content viral for their own AI agenda.

Literally, I think there is far… https://t.co/2sP45ylMJ6

— Mark Cuban (@mcuban) September 15, 2026
